title: Second Screwworm Case Confirmed in Webb County
excerpt: A second New World screwworm case has been confirmed in Webb County, with the U.S. Department of Agriculture dashboard showing two active cases in the county, according to KGNS.
content:
A second case of New World screwworm has been confirmed in Webb County, according to KGNS, prompting local leaders to urge ranchers and hunters to stay alert for signs of infection in animals.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture dashboard showed two active cases in the county as of Saturday, Nov. 21. The first case involved a calf in northern Webb County, which Webb Watch previously reported.

Webb County Commissioner John Galo said one of the affected ranches is near Mirando City. With deer season underway, Galo said it is important to reach hunters who may not live in the area, noting that Webb County draws many out-of-town hunters for its whitetail deer. He also urged ranchers to check their livestock daily for signs that an animal may need help.

Officials recommend calling a veterinarian immediately if an animal has a draining wound, maggots, or appears to be in discomfort. Getting help quickly can protect other animals and help prevent the spread, officials said.

The team of Webb County Judge-elect Jerry Garza said some ranches are under quarantine as leaders work to contain the cases.

Source: KGNS, Nov. 24, 2026.
